newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian troubled steel complex stops production.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian troubled steel complex stops production.

text.p: Nigeria's crisis-ridden steel complex in the midwestern town of Aladja has ceased production, the semi-official Daily Times newspaper on Monday.

Its investigations showed facilities at the multi-million naira Delta Steel Complex (DSC) were rusting away and the only functional structure was the air separation plant which taps natural air and converts it to gas.

The complex, commissioned in January 1982 and designed to produce one million tonnes of liquid steel per year, was one of two steel complexes expected to launch Nigeria into the league of steel-producing nations.

The other complex is being constructed in central Ajaokuta town and the military government announced in its fiscal budget in January that it was still committed to it and for which it provided 6.6 billion naira.
The paper said DSC produced only a total of 14,000 tonnes of liquid steel for four years before it stopped working in May.
The complex was overgrown with weeds and only a handful of staff report for duty, the paper said, adding that workers were being owed 10 months salaries in arrears.
DSC's general manager who declined to be named estimated that about $50 million would be required to make the complex functional again, the paper said.
A World Bank study on both projects at the time advised government against them, saying they were too expensive.
